question: Who among the following was a leader of Garam Dal, a group of radical nationalists?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bipin Chandra Pal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bipin Chandra Pal was one of the prominent leaders of the **Garam Dal** (Extremist faction) of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He was part of the famous triumvirate known as the **Lal-Bal-Pal trio**, which included Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal.
 
• The Garam Dal emphasized **direct action and self-reliance**, rejecting the moderate approach of petitions and prayers advocated by the Naram Dal (Moderates).
 
• Bipin Chandra Pal was a staunch advocate of **Swadeshi (use of Indian-made goods)** and Swaraj (self-rule).
 
• He played a significant role in the **Swadeshi Movement** of 1905, which was launched in response to the partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Garam Dal vs Naram Dal:**

 
 
• The Garam Dal (Extremists) advocated radical methods, including boycotts, protests, and mass mobilization, while the Naram Dal (Moderates) believed in dialogue and constitutional means.
 
• The split between the two factions became evident during the Surat Session of the Indian National Congress in 1907.
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement:**
 
 
• Launched in 1905, it aimed at promoting Indian goods and boycotting British products to strengthen India's economy.
 
• Bipin Chandra Pal actively campaigned for the movement through public speeches and writings.
 
 
 
• **Lal-Bal-Pal:**
 
 
• This trio of leaders symbolized the extremist phase of the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal were committed to achieving self-rule through assertive and revolutionary methods.
 
 
 
• **Partition of Bengal (1905):**
 
 
• Introduced by Lord Curzon, it divided Bengal into East and West regions, ostensibly for administrative efficiency but largely to weaken nationalist sentiments.
 
• The decision faced massive opposition, leading to the rise of the Swadeshi and Boycott movements.
 
 
 
• **Bipin Chandra Pal’s Contributions:**
 
 
• He was a writer, orator, and journalist who used his skills to inspire nationalist fervor.
 
• His publications included "New India" and "The Indian People," where he promoted his vision for an independent India.
